# Formation-coded Wilson hyperedge theorem — v0.4

Let `H_W` be the 152-dimensional integral Wilson orbital algebra frozen in `BASE/cap_hecke_152.npz`, and let

`R = (49,12,125,48,116,59,95)`

be the seven labelled Q192 routes: the C3 route 49 and the six directed C7 routes arranged in three transpose pairs.

## Theorem A — every route triple is complete by degree five
For every three-element subset `S` of `R`, the Q-linear algebra generated by the three orbital basis elements `{A_s : s in S}` is all of `H_W`. More strongly, words of length at most five already span all 152 dimensions.

The certificate is integral. For every one of the 35 triples, the word-coordinate matrix has rank 152 modulo `p=1,000,003`; the result is independently repeated at `p=1,000,033`. Since the coordinates and structure constants are integers, rank 152 modulo either prime exhibits a nonzero 152x152 integer minor. Hence the same word family has rank 152 over Q. The typical cumulative word dimensions are

`1, 4, 13, 40, 118–121, 152`

at lengths `0,1,2,3,4,5`.

## Theorem B — the Hamming/Fano mask is a complete-generator code
Let `C` be the binary `[7,4,3]` Hamming code, with its seven coordinates identified with the seven routes in `R`. Every nonzero word of `C` has weight 3, 4, or 7. Therefore every nonzero Hamming support contains a route triple, and Theorem A implies that **every nonzero formation-admissible Hamming mask generates the full Wilson algebra**. The seven minimum-weight words are the seven Fano lines; every one is a three-route, degree-five-complete Wilson instruction set.

## Formation interpretation
The mixed Schur-spectrum theorem supplied with the v0.4 handoff states, for pairwise nonisomorphic nonabelian simple species with multiplier C2, that `A_c in Form(G_N)` iff `c in N^perp`. Taking `N=C^perp` realizes exactly the Hamming code as the spectrum of central amalgams. Under that theorem, no singleton or pair mask occurs in the formation spectrum, while the seven Fano triples do occur. The Forge uses this spectrum as an exact higher-order architecture mask.

This last paragraph is an **imported working theorem interface**, not an independent proof audit of the new mixed formation theorem. The finite-field Hamming identities and the Wilson generation theorem are independently reproduced in this package. The mapping of seven formation coordinates to seven Wilson routes is an engineering identification, not an intrinsic isomorphism between the two finite-group constructions.
